exceptions.reason: Phase 1a E2.1 deliberately uses headless development tokens. These scenarios do not exercise Keycloak device authorization, URL/code presentation, browser approval, token polling or secure refresh-token storage. External browser UI remains manual coverage; development-token admission is not proof of the device flow.

subscope.scope: Remaining legacy E1.5 tags establish only authenticated behavior after development-token login: session replacement and movement rejection. They provide no device-flow coverage.

exceptions.reason: Headless development-token login and reconnect cover admission, not the story's click-login to external-browser approval and return-to-game UI. The external browser/UI portion remains manual coverage.

subscope.scope: Development-token login, play ticket, WebSocket admission, own spawn and reconnect projection rebuilding.

exceptions.reason: Evidence combines real-server late AOI entry/reconnect integration and a separate adversarial decoder replay. The live scenario does not deliver or inject an older-life server frame, so it cannot alone demonstrate stale-incarnation rejection. Logout can legitimately heal the NPC at home within the same life; reconnect compares the latest valid spawn with the projection, not the old wounds. XP is unknown until admission StatsChanged, which carries the authoritative total.

subscope.scope: The paired scenarios check wounded late-entry spawn projection, the next hit's HP continuity, reconnect life/fresh-spawn HP coherence and XP restoration. CapturedOlderLifeSpawnReplay replays admitted older-life wire bytes through the socket decoder after a newer life has live damage, asserting unchanged HP/cache/projection and no spawn callbacks. ReconnectNpcSpawnCoherence checks acceptance of same-life healing and rejection of incoherent HP or changed life. These are complementary test definitions, not an attestation that either suite has run.
